cues.text: Hello Eve, come in and sit down ... How’s it going?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Fine thanks. I’m looking forward to my teaching practice next week.
cues.speaker: Eve

cues.text: Good. Now you’ve got two classes, haven’t you - Year 3 and Year 6. Have you done your lesson plans?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Well, I’ve decided to take the topic of renewable energy ... I haven’t done a lesson plan for Year six yet, but I thought I’d base their lesson on an example of very simple technology. So I’ve brought this diagram to show you ... I got it from the Internet.
cues.speaker: Eve

cues.text: Let’s see ... A biogas plant ... So this is equipment for producing fuel from organic waste?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Yes. The smaller container on the left is where you put the waste you’ve collected ...
cues.speaker: Eve

cues.text: Right, and from there it’s piped into the larger tank?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: That’s right. And that’s slurry on the base of the larger tank.
cues.speaker: Eve

cues.text: Right ... and what exactly is slurry?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: It’s a mixture of organic waste and water.
cues.speaker: Eve

cues.text: So is that pipe at the bottom where the water comes in?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Yes it is ... As the slurry mixture digests it produces gas, and that rises to the top of the dome. Then when it’s needed it can be piped off for use as fuel in homes or factories. It’s very simple.
cues.speaker: Eve

cues.text: I suppose there’s some kind of safety valve to prevent pressure build-up?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: That’s the overflow tank. That container on the right. As the slurry expands some of it flows into that, and then once some of the gas has been piped off, the slurry level goes down again and the overflow tank empties again.
cues.speaker: Eve

cues.text: I see. Well I think that’s suitably simple for the age level it’s for. I look forward to seeing the whole lesson plan.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Thanks. And can I show you my ideas for the Year three lesson?
cues.speaker: Eve

cues.text: Of course. Let’s look.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: I thought I’d introduce the topic by writing the word ‘energy’ on the board, and reinforcing the spelling and the pronunciation. Then I’ll do a little mime - you know, run on the spot or something - to convey the sense.
cues.speaker: Eve

cues.text: I’d keep it brief at this stage ...
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Yes, I will. Then I’ll wipe the word off and write the question ‘Where does energy come from?’, and see what the pupils come up with.
cues.speaker: Eve

cues.text: Fine. I’d suggest that you just brainstorm at this stage, and don’t reject any of their suggestions.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Yes, that’s what I was going to do ... Then I’ve produced a set of simple statements, like ‘Energy makes cars move along the road’, and ‘Energy makes our bodies grow’. There are eight altogether.
cues.speaker: Eve

cues.text: Are you going to give them out as a handout? Or write them up on the board?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: First, I’ll put them on the board, and then I’ll read them out loud. And I’ll get the pupils to copy them out in their note books. I’ll also ask them to think up one more similar statement by themselves, and add it to the list.
cues.speaker: Eve

cues.text: Good idea.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: After that I thought I’d vary things a bit by sticking some pictures up ... of things like the sun and plants and food, and petrol, and a running child. And I’ll get the pupils to work out what order the pictures should come in, in terms of the energy chain.
cues.speaker: Eve

cues.text: I think that’s a very good idea. You could move the pictures around as the pupils give you directions.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Yes, I think they’d enjoy that. And to finish off I’ve made a gap-fill exercise to give out. They’ll be doing that individually, and while they’re writing I’ll walk round and check their work.
cues.speaker: Eve

cues.text: Good ... And have you worked out the timing of all that? It’ll probably take you right through to the end of the.
cues.speaker: Tutor
